title: cost-model-assumptions-internal-review-notes
content:
Internal review notes: cost model assumptions (data sources, calibration, finance sign-off)

Context:
- Purpose: capture open assumptions and calibration plan for the Optimize cost model spreadsheets (v3) before we request formal finance sign-off. This is a working doc — use as a checklist for the review meeting on 2026-03-15.
- Owner: Asha (product-optimize). Finance reviewer: Emma Caldwell. SRE reviewer: Rajiv. Engineering calibration: Liam, María.

Summary of high-level assumptions to review:
1) Unit cost basis
   - GPU hours: using list-price for p4d equivalent (baseline) and applying a blended discount factor for committed capacity. Current spreadsheet uses $3.20/hr (blended) — source: finance committed capacity export (billing_exposure_2025Q4.csv).
   - CPU (control plane) overhead: 0.08 $/req-hour equivalent (amortized). Source: infra-finance monthly summary (infra_costs_2025_11.xlsx).
   - Storage & network egress: $0.00012 per token (applied as per-token overlay). Source: cloud billing export + historical egress for hosted API (billing: hosted-usage-2025.csv).

2) Throughput & utilization assumptions
   - Baseline utilization (GPU active inference time / provisioned time): 62% (range tested 55–72%). Source: prometheus-inference-usage-2025-11 -> aggregated 30-day sliding window.
   - Effective qps per GPU depends on avg seq length and batching. We currently assume: avg seq length = 64 tokens; average generation tokens per request = 48. These come from sample of 10k requests in hosted-prod (sample_ids.csv).

3) Batching and caching effects
   - Batch size: default 8 for latency-sensitive routes, 32 for background. Assumption: batching increases throughput by 2.6x relative to batch=1 for our kernels. Source: serving-runtime perf runs (perf_batching_2025-10.log).
   - KV/prefix cache hit rate set to 18% for chat workloads. This is approximate — extracted from caching-traces-2025 Q4. Sensitivity: 5–30%.

4) Model quantization and perf multiplier
   - 4-bit quantized variant assumed to be 1.6x cheaper per token than fp16 (combo of raw FLOP reduction and memory throughput). Source: kernel-profiling-quant-4bit.csv and bench runs on p4d-sim.
   - Quality penalty assumptions: expected regression < 1.5% measured by eval suite default prompts. Need to confirm with research A/B.

5) Amortization & capital items
   - GPU amortization period: 36 months used in model. Finance noted 30–48 months are possible; amortization materially affects cost/active-hour.
   - Fraction of reserved vs spot used in Dedicated: spreadsheet assumes 70% reserved (committed), 30% spot. Need finance to confirm committed mix for new contracts.

Open data-source gaps / verification tasks:
- Reconcile blended GPU $/hr in spreadsheet with procurement contracts (finance to provide committed discount tiers by sku). (ACTION: Emma — due 2026-03-12)
- Confirm that prometheus-aggregates include pre-emption lost-time (we should subtract pre-emption recovery windows to get net usable hours). (ACTION: Rajiv — due 2026-03-12)
- Validate sample of token counts (10k sample) is representative across customers; run stratified sampling across top-20 tenants. (ACTION: Liam — due 2026-03-09)
- Get recent model profiling (per-token latency at seq len 16/64/256) for the quantized variants. (ACTION: María — due 2026-03-11)

Calibration plan (how to align model to billing):
Step 0: Snapshot current spreadsheets: cost-model-v3 (sheet id in linked_artifacts).
Step 1: Pull last 3 months of cloud billing exports (csv) and map to resource-level tags used by serving runtime (tag mapping table: infra_tag_map.xlsx).
Step 2: Pull production telemetry for same 3 months (prometheus series: gpu.active_seconds, inference.tokens_generated, inference.requests) and compute observed per-token cost by resource.
Step 3: Run reconciliation: compute modeled cost using our assumptions vs actual billed spend. Flag deltas > 10%.
Step 4: Sensitivity matrix: vary utilization +/-10pp, cache hit +/-10pp, batch factor +/-10% and compute range of modeled $/1M tokens. Create tornado chart.
Step 5: Propose final adjustments; get finance sign-off for amortization period and discount mix.

Calibration acceptance criteria (for finance sign-off):
- Modeled monthly spend within +/-10% of billed spend for 3 consecutive months OR
- Any larger delta must have a documented root cause and a mitigation plan (e.g., untagged resources, transient capacity events).
- Forecast accuracy for next quarter: modeled vs expected usage must be within 5% on token volume assumptions (finance to verify booking process).

Finance reviewer asks (explicit):
- Are we including indirect operating costs? (e.g., platform ops, monitoring, engineer time). Current model separates direct infra from SG&A to keep per-token cost invariant; but finance may require blended unit with overhead.
- How are customer committed discounts passed through? Do we amortize discounts only to Dedicated, or apportion across hosted customers?

Risks & conservative levers to recommend now:
- If amortization period is shortened to 30 months, unit cost increases ~8–12% depending on utilization.
- If cache hit is lower than assumed (<=10%), per-token cost could jump 6–10% for chat-heavy workloads.
- If quantized model needs more re-runs to hit same quality, net savings could be negative; require eval thresholds.

Draft recommendations (internal, not final):
1) Default to conservative amortization in public docs (36 months) but have finance sign-off path to adjust per-customer proposals.
2) Rollout conservative cache hit assumption in default templates: 12% for public docs; allow customers to supply telemetry to get custom numbers.
3) In spreadsheet, show both direct infra unit cost and an "all-in" unit cost that includes a 15% overhead for ops/support for sales conversations.
4) Add a scenario row for quantization tradeoffs: include expected quality delta and expected re-run multiplier.

Questions for meeting (2026-03-15):
- Finance: confirm blended GPU $/hr and reserved/spot mix for Dedicated baseline.
- SRE: can we produce hourly usable-GPU-hours (net of pre-emption) for the reconciliation window?
- Research: confirm that eval A/B for 4-bit quant will be completed by 2026-03-10; if not, we defer quant savings from the model.

Action items (owners + deadlines):
- Emma (Finance) — provide procurement discount sheet + preferred amortization policy — due 2026-03-12.
- Rajiv (SRE) — export net usable GPU hours and pre-emption logs for 2025-12..2026-02 — due 2026-03-12.
- Liam (Eng) — run stratified sampling of token lengths across top 20 tenants and update avg seq length table in spreadsheet — due 2026-03-09.
- María (Research) — provide per-model quantized perf/noise deltas and A/B artifact — due 2026-03-11.
- Asha (Product) — assemble reconciliation report and present at 2026-03-15 meeting (draft by 2026-03-13).

Appendix: quick math notes (for reference)
- modeled $/1M tokens = (GPU $/hr * hours_per_1M_tokens * (1 / utilization) + CPU_overhead + storage_egress_overlay) * (1 - cache_hit) * quant_multiplier
- hours_per_1M_tokens estimate: tokens_per_second_per_gpu * seconds_per_hour = tokens/hr. Inverse yields hours per 1M tokens. We calculate tokens/sec baseline at 25k tokens/sec for batch=8/seq=64 kernels -> ~40 GPU-hours per 1M tokens (sample).

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc focused on items that block finance sign-off; move longer sensitivity tables into the spreadsheet tab "sens_analysis_v3".
- Expect iteration — do not finalize amortization until finance confirms.

End of notes.
